land.text: Tula area: 'The area probably was under the political control of Teotihuacan in the Epiclassic period.'

predecessors.note: Cultural and regional predecessor only: Cliopatria's Teotihuacan ends in 704 and the Toltec begin in 875, so no land passes in a dated event.

capitals.name: Tollan-Xicocotitlan (Tula de Allende)
capitals.note: Toltec infobox: capital Tollan-Xicocotitlan. Tula page coordinates 20.0642 N, 99.3408 W. Tula Chico (abandoned between 850 and 900) and Tula Grande are two parts of one site. The Toltec page adds that recent scholarship doubts that Tula, Hidalgo was the Tollan of the Aztec accounts.

correction.text: Tula Chico 'grew into a small regional state out of the consolidation of the surrounding Coyotlatelco sites'; Tula Chico 'at its height spanned five to six km2' with 19,000-27,000 people, and Tula had 'another 20,000 to 25,000 in the surrounding 1000 km2'

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 5,605 km2 shape (bbox 99.08-98.18 W, 19.56-20.25 N) lies east of Tula and does not contain its cells (the gazetteer resolves Tula de Allende, 99.34 W, outside it). Corrected to a 20 km disc around Tula (about 1,250 km2, the page's 1,000 km2 hinterland). The Toltec infobox gives no area. The pages give no year for the state; Tula Chico was 'abandoned between 850 and 900CE', so 875 is Cliopatria's year, kept at confidence 1.

correction.text: 'Its political sphere is thought to include most of the present state of Hidalgo', possibly into the Valley of Mexico, the Toluca Valley and the Bajio; 'Tula probably did not rule an empire but may have ruled a regional state'

keyframe_review.note: Years 900-1150 only (Tula 'at its height between 900 and 1150'; 'Tula fell around 1150'). Cliopatria's 5,605 km2 shape misses Tula itself; Hidalgo is about 20,800 km2, a factor of 3.7 larger, but the page's sphere is explicitly soft ('thought to include'), so the rendering agent should draw it with a soft edge. The Toltec infobox gives no area; the Tula page gives 14 km2 for the city and 1,000 km2 around it. The Valley of Mexico, Toluca and Bajio are only 'possible' and are left out. The rest of Cliopatria's range (1151-1176) is not drawn.

correction.text: Not to be drawn: Tula fell around 1150 ('Many of the living quarters appear to have been abandoned by 1150'); no Toltec state is on the pages for 1177-1187

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1177-1187 shape has no support on the pages read. The Toltec infobox runs 'c. 950-1168' and the Tula page says the chronology 'dates the destruction of Tula to around 1179 under the rule of Ce Acatl Topilitzin. However, this story has been disputed.' The dossier ends in 1150 (the Tula page's archaeological date); a reviewer who prefers the traditional chronology would extend the end to 1168.

region.text: Tula Chico, a 'small regional state' of the consolidated Coyotlatelco sites

ledger.note: 875: the Tula Chico state at Tula, the seed of the Toltec. The Toltec page says Tula Chico 'grew into a small regional state out of the consolidation of the surrounding Coyotlatelco sites' but gives no year; 875 is Cliopatria's start (the Tula page has Tula Chico 'abandoned between 850 and 900CE').

region.text: 'its political sphere is thought to include most of the present state of Hidalgo'

ledger.note: 900: Tula Grande rises and the Toltec sphere spreads over most of Hidalgo. 'Tula Chico was abandoned between 850 and 900CE, and Tula Grande began to develop'; 'It reached its height between 900 and 1150.' The Toltec page puts prominence at 950-1150 (infobox c. 950-1168), so the year is the Tula page's and the extent is its 'thought to include'.

1150: Tula falls to Chichimec peoples and is abandoned. 'Tula fell around 1150'; 'There is evidence of the ceremonial center being burned in the 12th century.' The Toltec infobox gives 'Arrival of Chichimec peoples who conquered Tula' as the cause of collapse and c. 1168 as the end; the Tula page also mentions a disputed chronology of 1179. No successor state is named on either page.

wars.name: Chichimec conquest of Tula
wars.outcome: Tula was burned and abandoned in the 12th century; the Toltec page names 'Arrival of Chichimec peoples who conquered Tula' as the cause of collapse. No successor state holds the land on the pages read.
wars.note: The Tula page gives environmental stress around 1000 (soil leaching, drying climate) as pushing Chichimecs south and creating 'ethnic strife, which eventually resulted in the city's collapse', and does not say who burned the ceremonial centre. No land passes to a named state, so zones are empty.

certainty.note: Archaeological sphere of a regional state; the extent is only 'thought to include most of the present state of Hidalgo'. No border is known.

sources.title: Toltec
sources.note: Identity, capital Tollan-Xicocotitlan, infobox c. 950-1168, Tula Chico a small regional state, 'probably not deserving of being defined as an empire', Chichimec conquest as cause of collapse.

sources.title: Tula (Mesoamerican site)
sources.note: Dates (Tula Chico abandoned 850-900, height 900-1150, fell around 1150), city and hinterland size, political sphere 'most of the present state of Hidalgo', coordinates.

notes: Page budget 1-2 pages, two used. (1) Cliopatria's Toltec shape (5,605 km2, 99.08-98.18 W) lies east of Tula and does not contain it; corrected to a 20 km disc (875-899) and the state of Hidalgo (900-1150). (2) End date: 1150 (Tula page) against 1168 (Toltec infobox) and 1187 (Cliopatria); a disputed chronology puts the destruction in 1179. Not settled, the 1150 choice is a reading. (3) Start 875 is Cliopatria's and carries confidence 1; the Toltec infobox starts c. 950. (4) The Toltec page says recent scholarship doubts that Tula, Hidalgo was the capital of the Toltecs of the Aztec accounts (Teotihuacan proposed as the original Tollan); the dossier follows the archaeological Tula. (5) No ruler list is documented (Topiltzin is a mixture of ruler and god), so identity.rulers is omitted. (6) Native names are the place names given on the pages (Tollan, Tollan-Xicocotitlan); no Nahuatl name of the people was on a page read. (7) No named predecessor or successor state exists in Cliopatria; Teotihuacan (ends 704) is a cultural predecessor only.
